nodes.title: Foreign currency transactions and balances
nodes.summary:
Foreign currency transactions and balances
Transactions in foreign currencies are translated into respective functional currencies of Group Companies at exchange rates at the dates of the transactions. Monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies are translated into the functional currency at the exchange rate at the reporting date. Non-monetary items are measured at historical cost (translated using the exchange rates at the transaction date), except for non-monetary items measured at fair value which are translated using the exchange rates at the date when fair value was determined. Foreign exchange gains and losses resulting from the translation are recognised in the consolidated statement of profit and loss except for foreign currency exchange differences arising from the translation of the qualifying cash flow hedges to the extent that the hedges are effective.

nodes.title: Group Companies
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for group companies: foreign currency translation (assets/liabilities at closing rate, income/expenses at average rate, exchange differences in OCI, reclassification on disposal); inventories (measured at lower of cost and net realizable value, weighted average cost, inclusion of overheads, treatment of raw materials at replacement cost, and definition of stores/spares); government grants (recognition criteria, expense-related grants as income, asset-related grants as deferred income, and export entitlements as other operating revenue); and revenue recognition (sale of products including variable consideration, sales by clearing and forwarding agents, out-licensing arrangements with upfront fees, milestones, royalties, service fee revenue, and profit-sharing revenues).

nodes.title: Revenue Recognition Policies for Products, Licensing, and Services
key_items: Sales by clearing and forwarding agents
nodes.summary: The text outlines revenue recognition policies: product sales revenue is recorded at transaction price net of incentives and taxes, recognized upon control transfer, with variable consideration estimated using expected value or historical methods. Sales by clearing and forwarding agents are recognized upon delivery to distributors, with agents compensated on commission. Out-licensing arrangements include upfront payments, milestone payments, and royalties, with revenue recognized based on delivery, performance obligations, or accrual; variable consideration for sales-based milestones is estimated. Service fee revenue is recognized as services are performed, with upfront non-refundable payments deferred over the service period.

nodes.title: Profit sharing revenues
nodes.summary: The text describes profit sharing revenues from marketing arrangements where the Group sells products to business partners at a non-refundable base purchase price and is entitled to an additional profit share based on the partner's net sale proceeds or net profits, subject to adjustments. It explains that revenue equal to the base sale price is recognized upon delivery, while the profit share component is recognized only when highly probable that a significant reversal will not occur. The arrangements require partners to confirm units sold and net sales or net profit computations.

nodes.title: (vi) Contract balances
key_items: a) Employee’s provident fund; b) Gratuity obligations
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for contract balances, distinguishing contract assets (right to consideration for transferred goods/services before payment) and contract liabilities (obligation to transfer goods/services for consideration received/due, recognized as revenue upon performance). It details other income: interest income recognized on a time basis using the effective interest rate, dividend income when the right to receive is established, and other income (rent, insurance claims, vendor settlements, miscellaneous) when economic benefits are probable and measurable. Employee benefits include short-term benefits (salaries, wages, ex-gratia) recognized as services are rendered, and defined contribution plans (Employees' Pension Scheme, Labour Welfare Fund, ESIC, provident fund, USA 401(k), and other foreign plans) charged as contributions accrue. Defined benefit plans cover the employee provident fund (minimum return guarantee, actuarial valuation for shortfall) and gratuity (projected unit credit method, actuarial valuation, remeasurement in OCI, net interest cost, past service cost recognition).

nodes.title: Other benefit plans
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting for other benefit plans, specifically compensated absences and termination benefits. For compensated absences, liabilities due within one year are recognized at undiscounted estimated amounts, while those due beyond one year are actuarially valued using the projected unit credit method, with actuarial gains/losses immediately recognized in profit or loss. Termination benefits are recognized at the earlier of when the Group can no longer withdraw the offer or when it recognizes restructuring costs under Ind AS 37 involving such benefits. Benefits payable beyond 12 months are discounted to present value, with recognition in the consolidated statement of profit and loss.

nodes.title: Termination benefits
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting for employee benefits in consolidated financial statements: US subsidiaries' discretionary 401(k) contributions and foreign subsidiaries' defined contribution plans charged to profit or loss; defined benefit plans including the Employees' Provident Fund (monthly contributions to a trust, minimum government rate, shortfall as expense) and gratuity (actuarial valuation using projected unit credit method, remeasurements in OCI not reclassified, discounting using government bond yields, net interest cost in profit or loss, past service cost immediate recognition); other benefit plans for compensated absences (short-term undiscounted, long-term actuarial with immediate gains/losses); and termination benefits recognized when no longer withdrawable or upon restructuring under Ind AS 37, with long-term benefits discounted.

nodes.title: (vi) Other long-term employee benefits
key_items: a) Equity settled share-based payment transactions
b) Cash settled share-based payment transactions
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: other long-term employee benefits (discounted future benefits); share-based payments, both equity-settled (fair value expensed over vesting, proceeds to share capital/premium) and cash-settled (fair value expensed with liability remeasured); income taxes including current tax (rates enacted, offsetting) and deferred tax (temporary differences, asset recognition/review, MAT credit, liability for investments, offsetting, withholding tax on dividends); uncertain tax positions (accruals based on most likely or expected value); leases (right-of-use assets and lease liabilities recognition, measurement, depreciation, remeasurement, presentation); cash and cash equivalents (short-term highly liquid investments); provisions (present obligation, best estimate, discounting, onerous contracts); contingent liabilities and assets (disclosure, non-recognition); and financial instruments (initial recognition at fair value, subsequent classification into amortised cost, FVTOCI, FVTPL, and equity instruments at FVTOCI).

nodes.title: Provisions, Contingent Liabilities, and Financial Instruments Accounting Policies
nodes.summary: The page covers provisions for onerous contracts and subsequent measurement, contingent liabilities and assets, and financial instruments. It details recognition and measurement of provisions, including discounting and finance costs. Onerous contract provisions are recognized when expected benefits are lower than unavoidable costs, measured at present value of lower of termination or continuation costs, after impairing associated assets. Contingent liabilities are disclosed when outflow is not probable or estimable; contingent assets are not recognized but assessed continually for virtually certain inflows. Financial instruments section covers initial recognition at fair value (plus transaction costs for non-trade receivables), trade receivables at transaction price, subsequent measurement classification based on business model and cash flow characteristics into amortised cost, FVTOCI, FVTPL, and equity instruments at FVTOCI.

nodes.title: Debt instruments at amortised cost
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting for financial instruments under Ind AS 109. It details subsequent measurement of debt instruments at amortised cost using the effective interest rate (EIR) method, including treatment of discounts, premiums, fees, EIR amortisation in Other Income, and impairment losses in profit or loss. It describes debt instruments at fair value through other comprehensive income (FVTOCI), including initial and subsequent fair value measurement, recognition of fair value movements in OCI, interest income, impairment, foreign exchange in profit or loss, and reclassification on derecognition. It explains debt instruments at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL) as a residual category, including voluntary designation to avoid accounting mismatch, with fair value changes in profit or loss. It covers equity instruments measured at fair value, with held-for-trading classified as FVTPL, and an irrevocable election for other equity instruments to present fair value changes in OCI without recycling, except transfers within equity. Finally, it addresses derecognition of financial assets when contractual rights expire or rights are transferred under pass-through arrangements with transfer of risks, rewards, or control, including continued recognition with associated liability when involvement continues, and accounting for differences on full derecognition.

nodes.title: Classification and Measurement of Financial Instruments
key_items: Debt instrument at fair value through other comprehensive income (FVTOCI)
Debt instrument at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL)
nodes.summary: The text covers the classification and measurement of three types of financial instruments: debt instruments at fair value through other comprehensive income (FVTOCI), debt instruments at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL), and equity instruments. For FVTOCI debt instruments, it details initial and subsequent fair value measurement, recognition of fair value movements in OCI, interest income, impairment, and foreign exchange in profit or loss, and reclassification on derecognition. For FVTPL debt instruments, it explains the residual category, optional designation to avoid accounting mismatch, and fair value measurement with changes in profit or loss. For equity instruments, it covers fair value measurement, classification of held-for-trading as FVTPL, irrevocable election for FVTOCI on instrument-by-instrument basis, treatment of fair value changes including foreign exchange and dividends, no recycling, and transfer within equity, while FVTPL equity instruments recognize all changes in profit or loss.

nodes.title: (c) De-recognition

It addresses continued recognition to the extent of continuing involvement with associated liabilities, and gain/loss recognition in profit or loss upon full de-recognition. It also details impairment of financial assets using the expected credit loss model under Ind AS 109, applying the simplified approach for trade receivables with a provision matrix based on historical default rates adjusted for forward-looking estimates. Finally, it covers financial liabilities: initial recognition and classification (FVTPL, loans, borrowings, payables, hedging derivatives), subsequent measurement at amortized cost or FVTPL, specific treatment of FVTPL liabilities including own credit risk in OCI, and amortized cost measurement using the effective interest rate method with interest expense in finance costs.

nodes.title: Financial liabilities subsequently measured at amortised cost

It then discusses derivative financial instruments for hedge accounting, classifying hedges as fair value hedges (using forward contracts for foreign currency risk) and cash flow hedges (using forwards, options, and swaps for foreign currency and interest rate risk), with rules for gains/losses, ineffective portions, and hedge discontinuation. Finally, it covers financial guarantee contracts, initially measured at fair value and subsequently at the higher of expected credit loss or initial amount less cumulative income.

nodes.title: Financial Liabilities, Derivatives, and Hedge Accounting Policies
nodes.summary: The page covers amortized cost calculation using the effective interest rate method. It addresses de-recognition of financial liabilities, including discharge, cancellation, expiration, and replacement or modification. It details derivative financial instruments for hedge accounting, classifying hedges as fair value hedges (for changes in fair value of recognized assets/liabilities or firm commitments) and cash flow hedges (for variability in cash flows or foreign currency risk). Fair value hedges use forward contracts, initially and subsequently measured at fair value, with gains/losses in profit or loss, and hedge accounting discontinued under specified conditions. Cash flow hedges use forwards, options, and swaps, with effective portions in other comprehensive income and accumulated in hedging reserve, ineffective portions in profit or loss, and reclassification to profit or loss when hedged items affect profit or loss, with treatment upon expiry, sale, termination, or forecast transaction changes.

nodes.title: (iv) Financial guarantee contracts

nodes.title: Independent Assurance Statement*
nodes.summary: The Independent Assurance Statement by DNV covers Cipla's sustainability non-financial disclosures in its Integrated Report FY 2024-25, including limited assurance for GRI disclosures and reasonable assurance for specific GRI 302, 303, 305, 306, and 418 disclosures under BRSR Core across global operations. It details reporting criteria, assurance methodology, and basis of conclusion, including risk-based approach, data verification, interviews, and site audits. The conclusion evaluates DNV VeriSustainTM principles (Materiality, Responsiveness, Reliability/Accuracy, Completeness, Neutrality) with no significant issues. It outlines responsibilities of Cipla and DNV, use and distribution restrictions, and inherent limitations such as ±5% uncertainty, exclusion of financial data, future statements, strategy, other frameworks, and legal compliance.

nodes.title: Independent Assurance Statement for Cipla's Sustainability Disclosures
nodes.summary: DNV conducted an independent assurance of Cipla's sustainability non-financial disclosures in its Integrated Report FY 2024-25. The scope includes limited assurance for GRI disclosures and reasonable assurance for specific GRI 302, 303, 305, 306, and 418 disclosures under BRSR Core, covering global operations. Reporting criteria include GRI Standards 2021, IIRC's Integrated Reporting framework, UN SDGs, and GHG Protocol. DNV's competence and independence are ensured through ISO/IEC 17029:2019-based quality control, compliance with ethical requirements, and no conflict of interest. The assurance methodology follows DNV's VeriSustainTM Protocol V6.0, ISAE 3000 (revised), ISO 14064-3, and ISO 14046.

nodes.title: Basis of our conclusion
nodes.summary: The text outlines the basis of a conclusion from an assurance process by a multi-disciplinary team for selected Cipla sites. It details activities including: adopting a risk-based approach focused on material issues; reviewing general, GRI-specific, and other key disclosures; understanding systems, processes, and controls for non-financial reporting; conducting walk-throughs and sample-based testing of data processes; collecting documentary evidence and management representations; interviewing senior managers responsible for disclosures; conducting on-site audits at corporate offices and sites with sample-based assessment; reviewing reporting processes against assessment criteria; interviewing managers and reviewing evidence for environmental KPIs; and verifying consolidated performance disclosures for completeness under the VeriSustainTM Protocol for limited assurance.

nodes.title: Our Conclusion:
nodes.summary: The text presents an assurance conclusion on Cipla's GRI disclosures, finding nothing to suggest unfair statement. It evaluates five DNV VeriSustainTM principles: Materiality (double materiality assessment, no significant change in topics), Responsiveness (policies and mechanisms for stakeholder issues), Reliability/Accuracy (data verification with minor inaccuracies corrected), Completeness (reporting of material ESG issues within boundary), and Neutrality (balanced presentation). It outlines responsibilities of Cipla (report preparation, data quality) and DNV (independent opinion, liability disclaimer), use and distribution restrictions, and inherent limitations including a ±5% uncertainty, exclusion of financial data, future statements, strategy, other frameworks, and legal compliance. The statement is signed by DNV with date and location.

nodes.title: Assurance Statement Responsibilities and Usage Terms
key_items: Use and distribution of Assurance statement
nodes.summary: The page outlines the division of responsibilities and terms of use for an assurance statement related to Cipla's report. It begins with a brief mention of the report's content and presentation within macroeconomic and industry contexts, and notes no issues with the Principle of Neutrality. The 'Responsibility of the Company' section states Cipla is solely responsible for report preparation, information disclosure, processes for data collection and reporting, information quality and consistency, and website integrity. 'DNV’s Responsibility' clarifies DNV's responsibility to management, presents its independent opinion for stakeholders, and disclaims liability for decisions based on the statement. 'Use and distribution of Assurance statement' restricts the statement's use to the company per agreement, disclaims responsibility to third parties, limits conclusions to the report, and specifies that use is governed by the contract, with no liability for alternative purposes.

nodes.title: Inherent Limitations
nodes.summary: The text outlines DNV's assurance engagement limitations: reliance on good-faith, complete, and authentic data; a ±5% uncertainty threshold for errors/omissions; exclusion of financial data evaluation (relying on third-party audited reports); scope limited to the defined reporting period and operations boundary; exclusion of opinions, beliefs, future intentions, intellectual property, and competitive issues; no review of strategy or related linkages; no mapping to other reporting frameworks; exclusion of legal compliance; and provides assurance team details and signatories.

nodes.title: Annexure I

Footnotes detail energy data (I-RECs, assurance boundary), Scope 1 and 2 GHG calculation methodologies (IPCC, CEA, EPA, etc.), and Scope 3 categories and tools (IPCC, GaBi, USEEIO, DEFRA, GHG Protocol, IEA).

It outlines DNV's competence, independence, and methodology using VeriSustainTM and ISAE 3000, including basis of conclusion, inherent limitations, and responsibilities. It covers use and distribution terms, signatories, and Annexure I specifying BRSR Core and other disclosures, with footnotes on energy and GHG methodologies.

nodes.title: Basis of our conclusion
key_items: BRSR Core Indicators – Reasonable level of Assurance
nodes.summary: A multi-disciplinary team of assurance specialists conducted assurance work for selected Cipla sites, providing reasonable assurance on BRSR Core indicators across nine ESG attributes. They reviewed disclosures, evaluated design and implementation of systems, processes, and controls, assessed operational control and reporting boundaries, gathered extensive evidence, and engaged stakeholders. The DNV audit team performed on-site audits for data testing, assessed uniformity in reporting processes, and conducted quality checks at locations selected based on contribution to reported indicators, operational complexity, and reporting systems. DNV also interviewed senior managers responsible for disclosures and reviewed evidence supporting environmental KPIs, and verified consolidated performance disclosures for completeness under the VeriSustainTM Protocol V6.0 for both reasonable and limited assurance.

nodes.title: Inherent Limitations
key_items: Rest non-financial disclosures in BRSR – Limited Level of Assurance
nodes.summary: The text outlines DNV's assurance engagement limitations, emphasizing reliance on company-provided data, a ±5% materiality threshold, and exclusion of financial data evaluation (except reliance on third-party audits for specific BRSR Core indicators). It details a limited level of assurance for non-financial BRSR disclosures, covering general disclosures, management processes, and principle-wise performance, using a risk-based approach with site audits and sample testing. The scope excludes data outside the reporting period or operational boundary, opinions, future intentions, intellectual property, strategy, other frameworks, and legal compliance. Responsibilities are assigned to Cipla for report preparation and to DNV for the independent opinion, with strict use and distribution terms limiting liability to the company. The text concludes with signatories and the assurance team.

nodes.title: BRSR Assurance Scope and Responsibilities
nodes.summary: The page outlines the scope and responsibilities for a BRSR assurance engagement. It states that aspects outside the defined scope and boundary are not assured and that the assessment is limited to defined parameters. Legal compliance is excluded, with the Company responsible for adherence to laws. The 'Responsibility of the Company' section details Cipla's sole responsibility for preparing the BRSR, including information in BRSR Core and BRSR, maintaining processes for collecting, analyzing, and reporting information, ensuring quality and consistency, and maintaining website integrity and referenced disclosures. The 'DNV's Responsibility' section states DNV's responsibility is to Management, that its statement is an independent opinion for stakeholders, and that DNV disclaims liability for decisions based on the assurance statement.

nodes.title: GRI Content Index
nodes.summary: This GRI Content Index details Cipla Limited's sustainability reporting for April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025, in accordance with GRI Standards. It lists disclosures for GRI 2: General Disclosures (organizational details, governance, strategy, policies, compliance, stakeholder engagement, etc.) and GRI 3: Material Topics, including management approach. The index covers specific material topics: Access and Affordability of Medicines, Product Quality and Safety (GRI 416, 417), Data Privacy and Cyber Security (GRI 418), Innovation and R&D, Sustainable Supply Chain (GRI 204, 308, 407, 408, 409, 414), Corporate Governance and Business Ethics (GRI 201, 205, 206), Occupational Health and Safety (GRI 403), Human Capital Management (GRI 401, 402, 404, 405, 406, 407, 408, 409, 410), Climate Action and Resource Management (GRI 201, 302, 303, 304, 305, 306), Community Wellbeing (GRI 413), and Technology and Digitalisation. Each disclosure is mapped to its location in the annual report or other documents.

nodes.title: Disclaimer
nodes.summary: This disclaimer covers forward-looking statements and associated risks/uncertainties (strategy implementation, growth, regulatory approvals, tech changes, earnings/forex fluctuations, international operations, market risks, pandemic impact). It states Cipla Limited has no obligation to update such statements. It clarifies the annual report is not for endorsing/advertising products, notes 'g'/'generic' indicate generic versions of brand drugs, and provides medical product/device information for general purposes only, varying by country and dependent on patents/marketing authorisations. It advises independent availability enquiries per country, states the information is not complete medical information or a substitute for consulting qualified doctors, and is not advice or a recommendation for decisions/actions.

structure.title: Letter to shareholders.pdf
structure.summary: This document is a letter from Cipla Limited inviting members to the 89th Annual General Meeting (AGM) scheduled for July 16, 2025, via video conferencing. It provides the company's registration details, including CIN, address, contact information, and website. The letter explains that the AGM Notice and Integrated Annual Report for FY 2024-25 are being sent via email to registered members. For members without a registered email, it provides QR codes, web links, and paths to access the AGM Notice and Integrated Annual Report. It also mentions that details on e-voting, attending the AGM through VC, dividend entitlement, and TDS on dividend are in the AGM Notice. The letter is signed by Rajendra Chopra, Company Secretary, dated June 19, 2025, in Mumbai.
